where: retained distributed libraries, source ownership helpers and the harness UI error boundaries
what: The imported untyped-error ratchet refused 12 crate/column groups. Native pack validation, compiler callbacks and service startup had flattened distinct failures into String or anyhow, and new source/metadata/UI helpers repeated that contract.
cost: CI could not accept the retained V2 libraries; callers could only classify several data-integrity and startup failures by parsing their rendered messages.
cause: The public interfaces described presentation text rather than the operation's failure data, so each implementation discarded the original cause before its caller could inspect it.
whys: The gate found untyped errors in newly retained APIs.
The APIs required rendered strings or a fully erased error.
Compiler callback trait signatures forced every implementation to erase its own error type.
Neither the type boundary nor the earlier branch's checks required a matchable refusal with its input context.
class: error interfaces erase failure identity before the reporting boundary
prevention: Compiler callbacks require an associated std::error::Error type and retain trait-object support. Pack, manifest, publication, admission, metadata and UI refusals carry typed causes and their digest, location, address or path. Existing strict untyped-error checks remain enabled; no allowance was raised.
fix: Implemented the typed interfaces and all callers. Existing refusal tests now match variants; new controls exercise manifest parsing causes and a real occupied listening address. Existing driver and grant controls explicitly pass typed-error trait objects. The full native library and all-target compile checks are requested from the main lane.
state: Native run 44982739668 at 47ef316 passed the strict untyped-error gate with every crate at its exact existing row. All 119 distributed library tests passed, including the two new typed-refusal controls. All 47 memo integration tests, three shared-source compiler cache-key controls and three standalone browser-origin tests passed. The expanded all-target compile exposed an unrelated missing Ack import in the Unix integration test; that import is repaired for the next run. Full desktop and parked-compiler compilation remains unestablished.
